stories.headline: A long-delayed bridge over the Yalu River opens
stories.summary: A new road bridge across the Yalu River has opened between Dandong in China and Sinuiju in North Korea, following a 12-year delay. The cable-stayed bridge is 3 km long, including the supporting roads. It replaces the Sino-Korean Friendship Bridge, which opened in 1943 and is wide enough for only a single rail track and a single reversible lane.

stories.headline: Ireland's public sector holds its first general strike since 2009
stories.summary: Approximately 300,000 workers across Ireland's public sector have begun nationwide industrial action. Teachers, health workers and other civil servants joined, after negotiations with the government on a new public service pay agreement fell through. It is the country's first general strike since 2009, and further strikes are planned for 21 October.

stories.headline: Severe drought is declared across six English counties
stories.summary: The United Kingdom has declared a severe drought in Cornwall, Devon, Dorset, Somerset, East Sussex and West Sussex. Prolonged low rainfall has left more than 80% of England in drought, with major reservoirs below 20% capacity. The 2026 drought escalated rapidly after an extraordinarily dry and hot summer.

stories.headline: Timekeepers vote to stop adding leap seconds
stories.summary: The General Conference on Weights and Measures has voted to discontinue future leap seconds, the one-second adjustments that kept clocks in step with the turning Earth. Coordinated Universal Time becomes continuous from 20 May 2027. The leap second was introduced in 1972, and 27 of them were added in all, the last on 31 December 2016.
